source.notes: Single PDF (code 'T26 521 – SPECIMEN', printed footer) contains both the Question Paper (17 printed pages) and a 'DRAFT MARKING SCHEME' (5 printed pages). Found on the official specimen-papers listing page https://cisce.org/specimen-question-papers-icse-class-x-2026-2/ ; the specimen is published for the ICSE 2026 examination, so examYear is 2026. Maximum Marks 80, Time allowed Two hours; first 15 minutes are reading time only. PDF page numbers do NOT equal the printed page numbers: PDF page 2 is an unnumbered 'NOTE' insert page (about the specimen paper's purpose), so printed page N (N>=2) sits on PDF page N+1; the question paper spans PDF pages 1-18 (printed '1 of 17' to '17 of 17') and the marking scheme spans PDF pages 19-23 (printed '1 of 5' to '5 of 5'). The 'page' field on each question below is the PDF page number. Official ExamReady field 'session' set to a descriptive label because no exam session (e.g. 'March 2026') is printed. Structure: SECTION A (40 Marks) is compulsory - Question 1 (15 one-mark MCQ/assertion-reason sub-parts (i)-(xv)), Question 2 ([6] one-mark fill-in-the-blank sub-parts under (i), a [2] match-the-column (ii), and a [2] short-answer (iii)), and Question 3 (seven sub-questions (i)-(vii) totalling 15 marks). SECTION B (40 Marks) prints 'Attempt any four questions from this Section' and offers six 10-mark questions (Question 4 - Question 9); this pack extracts ALL SIX Section B questions (60 marks) because the choice is of whole questions, not internal alternatives, so the pack's marks total (100) intentionally exceeds maxMarks (80) - a student scores at most 80 by answering 40 (Section A) + 40 (best 4 of 6 Section B questions, 10 each). No question in this paper prints an internal-choice 'OR' between alternative sub-parts, so choiceGroup is null throughout. Where a single printed mark bracket (e.g. '[3]') covers two or more lettered sub-parts and the marking scheme does not print a mark against each sub-part individually, the total was split across the sub-parts based on the relative complexity/number of steps shown in the marking scheme working; this is flagged per question and confidence is set to MEDIUM. Several marking-scheme phrases use an embedded math-italic font whose glyphs did not map to correct Unicode in the PDF text layer: a genuine single-letter variable (e.g. 't', 'v', 'R') consistently extracts as that same character doubled and was decoded by removing the duplicate; a multi-letter word extracts as a single wrong glyph repeated 2x-the-letter-count times (e.g. a 7-repeat-14 run decoding to 'Voltage', a 9-repeat-18 run decoding to 'secondary') - where letter-count and surrounding physics vocabulary made the intended word unambiguous it was reconstructed and flagged per-question with MEDIUM confidence (e.g. Q1(xii)'s transformer options, decoded as 'Voltage/Current/number of turns/Power' x 'primary/secondary'); where a derivation's wording could not be reliably reconstructed (e.g. the parenthetical remark in Q8(iii)(d)) it was left out and flagged, keeping only the clearly-extracted final results/numbers per the pack rules (no derivations were invented). Figures, circuit diagrams, ray diagrams and graphs are never reproduced; each affected question is flagged with hasFigure true and an extractionIssues entry. Cognitive-level tags ('[Application]', '[Recall]', combined tags like '[Recall & Understanding]', etc.) are printed in the right margin of the question paper; the raw (non -layout) text extraction places all of a page's tags together in question order at the end of the page content, which was used to assign each tag to its sub-part in the same top-to-bottom order print on that page (this is unambiguous and was cross-checked page by page). Usage: Official CISCE publication, freely available on cisce.org; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text: Anita used a single movable pulley to lift a bucket of water from a well. She lubricates the pulley. Which of the following statements is true regarding the performance of the pulley used?

A solid of mass 60 g at 100°C is placed in 150 g of water at 20°C. The final steady temperature is 25°C. Calculate the heat capacity of the solid.
[sp. heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹]

officialAnswer.text:
By principle of mixtures, Heat lost = Heat gained
(m × c × ΔT) metal = (m c ΔT) water
c’ × 75 = 150 × 4.2 × 5
c’ = 42 J K⁻¹

A scientist lowers a metallic ruler vertically into a transparent oil tank. The ruler touches an object placed at the bottom of the tank and gets wet up to the 25 cm mark. If the refractive index of the glycerin is 1.25:

extractionIssues: The printed [3] mark bracket covers both (a) and (b) of this item; the split is not printed; 2 marks assigned to (a) and 1 mark to (b), matching the multi-step calculation in (a).

questions.text: A, B, C and D are four points on a hemispherical cup placed inverted on the ground. Diameter BC = 360 cm and AE = R/3 (R is the radius of the cup). A small spherical mass 500 g at rest at the point A, slides down along the smooth surface of the cup. Assuming that there is no loss of energy, calculate its Speed at the point B (lowest point).

officialAnswer.text:
Using energy conservation, PE at A = KE at B ⇒ mgh = ½ mv²
v = √(2gh) = √(2×10×1.8) = 6 m/s

figures.alt: Inverted hemispherical cup with points A, B, C, D and E, base BC marked 360 cm and AE marked R/3

questions.text: A, B, C and D are four points on a hemispherical cup placed inverted on the ground. Diameter BC = 360 cm and AE = R/3 (R is the radius of the cup). A small spherical mass 500 g at rest at the point A, slides down along the smooth surface of the cup. Assuming that there is no loss of energy, calculate its Kinetic Energy at D (g = 10 ms⁻²).

officialAnswer.text:
Height above B = 2R/3 = 1.2 m
P.E. at D = mgh = 0.5 × 10 × 1.2 = 6 J
K.E. at D = TE − PE at D = 9 − 6 = 3 J

figures.alt: Inverted hemispherical cup with points A, B, C, D and E, base BC marked 360 cm and AE marked R/3

questions.text:
The given diagram shows the output of an AC generator. If the speed of the generator coil is doubled, then:
(b) what is the effect on the physical quantity indicated as ‘b’?
(c) give reason for your answer in (b).

officialAnswer.text: If speed is doubled, it means time of a cycle will be halved.
